title: What if only you exist and everyone turns into zombies
idea: What if only you exist in the world, and everyone transforms into zombies

cast.name: You
cast.look: young survivor in a blue hoodie, dark pants, sneakers, small backpack

scenes.title: The Silent Morning
scenes.goal: You wake up. The world is wrong.

cues: You wake up to a silence so deep it hurts.
No cars. No birds. No alarm clocks in the building.
You check your phone. Four hundred missed calls, all from the same night.
The last message from your mother says only: do not open the door.
You are about to find out why.
You pull back the curtain and your stomach drops.
The street is full of people, standing perfectly still.
Hundreds of them, heads tilted, eyes empty, all facing your window.
One of them slowly raises an arm and points at you.
Then, together, they begin to walk.
The news channel is still broadcasting, on a loop, from the night before.
A calm voice explains that something spread while the world slept.
Everyone who was asleep changed. Everyone who was awake changed faster.
You were the only one who took the pill that night.
The doctor's pill for your insomnia. The pill that saved you.
You slip into the cafe downstairs and watch through the glass.
A zombie bumps a chair, and the whole crowd turns toward the sound.
They don't see well. They hear everything.
So rule one is simple: silence. Soft shoes, slow steps, no panic.
Even your heartbeat feels too loud.
By noon you have a backpack, bottled water, and a flashlight.
You find a bicycle, but bicycles click, so you leave it.
You find a radio and turn the volume down to nothing.
Static. Static. Then, very faintly, a voice counting numbers.
Somebody else is out there. Somebody is alive.
You climb to the rooftop and tune the radio by hand.
The voice repeats: north tower, sunrise, bring nothing loud.
Below you, the crowd drifts like a slow river.
Crossing the city will take all night, and you've never felt so small.
But hope is a strange kind of fuel.
You walk through the park at dusk, breathing through your sleeve.
A zombie stands under a streetlight, humming a lullaby.
You freeze. The melody sounds like your grandmother's song.
It is only a memory in a broken mind, but it still stings.
You step around it, and it never turns.
At last you reach the north tower, and the lobby is empty.
Chairs stacked against the doors. Candles still warm on a desk.
A note reads: we left at dawn, we are sorry, we waited.
You missed them by minutes. Your knees give out.
Then you hear footsteps behind you. Slow ones.
You turn around, ready to run, but it's the voice from the radio.
An old man in a lab coat, calm and unafraid.
He says: they were never hunting you. They were guarding you.
The ones who changed still remember the last thing they loved.
And the last thing they all loved was keeping the sleeper safe.
On the roof, the sun rises over a quiet, strange city.
Down in the street, the crowd gathers and simply watches over you.
You are not the last human. You are the last who can choose.
The old man hands you the cure, one dose, one chance.
Would you use it, or would you let them stay?
The world did not end that night. It went quiet, and taught you to listen.
You learned patience and fear, and what you would protect.
Being alone is scary, but it also shows what matters.
The people you love don't disappear when the world changes.
They hold on in ways that you may never notice.
So tell me in the comments: would you use the cure?
Like and follow for the next what-if story.
